ideas.title: QR Stickers That Open the Right Page of the Home Guide
ideas.why: Home-record apps like Equipment Tracker, JustTaggit and Essentify put a QR sticker on the water heater, furnace or panel so anyone can scan it with a phone camera, no app needed, and land on that unit's page (model, manual, service history). The Home Guide is already the most-used app (20 sign-ins, 13 Home section opens, 6 Who to Call, 5 Warranty, 3 Shutoffs in the last usage pull), but the guide has no per-section links yet, so a sticker can only open the front door. Giving each section its own link and printing 5 to 8 stickers for Niko's mechanical room would put the answer on the equipment itself. Sign-in stays as is, so no private info is exposed.

source.title: Equipment Tracker: QR Tags on Your Equipment

mockup: Sticker on water heater: 'Scan for manual, warranty and shutoff'
After sign-in: Water Heater card with model, warranty end date, flush steps, who to call
Same pattern for the furnace, electrical panel, main water shutoff and other mechanical-room equipment

ideas.title: Talk Instead of Type at Each Stop
ideas.why: CompanyCam's Quick Caption lets crews tap a mic after a photo and say what it shows; its Walkthrough Note turns spoken notes plus photos into an editable document, and CompanyCam pitches it as safer than typing on site. Site Walk asks the walker to label photos and write notes at 7 stops, and the last usage pull shows Stop 1 started 8 times but only 1 finished walk, so typing on a phone may be part of the drop-off (unconfirmed). A mic button on each Notes box using the browser's built-in dictation would cut typing without any AI cost.

source.title: CompanyCam AI User Guide: Quick Caption and Walkthrough Note

ideas.before: Type every note on the phone keyboard while holding the camera
ideas.after: Tap the mic, say 'water shutoff behind the furnace, red handle', words appear in Notes, edit if needed

ideas.title: Missed Words Come Back Sooner
ideas.why: The quiz now has 94 active words and a Known Words list, but every word gets the same turn. FSRS is the free, open-source scheduler that Anki-style apps use: each answer moves a word's next review date, so missed words return within minutes and easy ones fade out for days. ts-fsrs is an MIT-licensed JavaScript version that can run in the page and save progress in the browser, so no server is needed. It's Max's own app, so it could ship as soon as he says yes.
steps: Each word gets a small review record saved on the phone
After each answer, rate it Again, Hard, Good or Easy (or auto-rate from right or wrong)
The app shows 'Due today: 12 words' and quizzes those first
Missed words reappear in the same session; known words drift to weeks out
Share button sends the due count and hardest words to Thai

ideas.title: Address Suggestions on the First Step
ideas.why: Step 1 of the Smart Upkeep funnel is a free-text 'Address or ZIP' box that pulls the ZIP out with a pattern match and warns if it's outside metro Detroit. Baymard's checkout testing found typed addresses cause frequent errors that slow or stop people, that live address suggestions were the best-performing fix, and that 55% of sites still don't offer them. Suggestions would give a clean ZIP for the service-area check and a verified service address for later steps. It needs an address lookup service (for example Google Places), which has usage costs, so Up Keep should price that first.

source.title: Baymard: Provide Fully Automatic Address Lookup

ideas.before: Type '123 Main St, Novi' or a ZIP; the app guesses the ZIP from the text
ideas.after: Type '123 Ma...', pick the suggested full address, and see 'In our service area' right away

ideas.title: Same Named Tech Every Visit
ideas.why: Honey Homes sells its membership on one dedicated handyman who learns your home and comes back each visit. For the 48322 friends-and-family beta, a named tech is the cheapest retention and trust lever (estimate: no extra cost while volume is under one tech's capacity). Impact: High (retention, trust).
ideas.before: Any available tech, introduced on arrival
ideas.after: 'Your tech: Dana' card with photo; same person every visit, backup named too

ideas.title: Partner Vetting Checklist Before Any Sub Works
ideas.why: Michigan's workers' comp agency says a general contractor should require a WC certificate or exclusion from subs, or the sub's injured employee's claim can become the contractor's responsibility. This is the concrete answer to 'how to source and subcontract techs' for HVAC and anything over the $600 M&A line. Impact: High (legal risk).
steps: Check license status on LARA (M&A, Mechanical, Plumbing, Electrical)
Collect a current workers' comp certificate or a filed WC-337 exclusion
Collect general liability and auto certificates, naming the operator as additional insured
Re-check every expiry date monthly; block scheduling if anything lapses

ideas.title: Michigan 3-Day Cancel Notice for In-Home Sign-Ups
ideas.why: Michigan's Home Solicitation Sales Act lets buyers cancel within 3 business days when the sale is made at their home (over $25), and requires a specific bold notice next to the signature. Beta members will often sign during the first walkthrough visit, so the agreement needs it. For the lawyer review already on the list. Impact: High (compliance).
ideas.after: Signature step shows the statutory 3-business-day cancel line in bold, plus a dated cancel form emailed with the agreement

ideas.title: Builder and Closing Handoff Channel
ideas.why: Digs raised $25.3M (Aug 2026) led by Builders FirstSource to carry a home's digital record from construction into post-move-in maintenance and warranty care. Builders want a homeowner handoff; for SmartKeep it is a path to the first 100 homes and to US LOIs before Nov 8. Impact: High (acquisition).
steps: List 5 metro Detroit custom builders and 5 listing agents in 48322
Offer a gifted first visit plus a set-up Home Record at closing
Builder's warranty items load into the record
Track how many gifts convert to paid tiers (estimate goal: 1 in 4)

ideas.title: Maintenance Proof Pack for Warranty Claims
ideas.why: The FTC warns home warranty claims are often denied over exclusions and missing maintenance. A one-tap dated, photo-backed service history per appliance makes the membership pay for itself when a claim happens, a trust message warranties can't offer. Impact: Medium (trust, retention).

source.title: FTC: What's the Deal With Home Warranties?

ideas.title: Annual Background Re-Check, Shown to Members
ideas.why: Thumbtack runs a criminal background check on every new pro through an accredited third party and re-checks annually. Monthly Platinum visits put someone in the home 12 times a year; stating the check and its date is a simple trust signal for 3,500–5,000 sq ft homes. Impact: Medium (trust).

ideas.title: Tap to Verify the License
ideas.why: Michigan's LARA lookup shows status and expiry for mechanical, plumbing, electrical and M&A licenses, updated daily. Tagging each task Member Tech vs Licensed Sub and linking the live license turns the licensing problem into a visible trust feature. Impact: High (trust, licensing).

ideas.title: Failed Card Recovery From Day One
ideas.why: Stripe's revenue recovery tools retry failed subscription payments and email customers with no code. Stripe cites about 55% recovery on average; an independent B2C audit reports 25–35%. Either way, monthly billing without dunning quietly loses members. Fits the Stripe setup already on the open list. Impact: Medium (retention).
steps: Turn on Stripe Smart Retries (default 8 tries in 2 weeks)
Send card-expiring and payment-failed emails with a hosted update link
Pause scheduling, don't cancel, while a payment is in recovery
Watch the Recovery Rate chart monthly

ideas.title: Renewal Rate Tracker Against the 80% Bar
ideas.why: Frontdoor, the largest US home warranty company, reported 79.2% customer retention for 2025. An internal operator view of upcoming renewals, skipped visits and at-risk members gives the SMART-S file real retention data and catches churn early. Internal only, no client data in marketing. Impact: Medium (retention, evidence).

ideas.title: Hand the Home Record to the Next Owner
ideas.why: Digs pitches a home record that 'lives on well past the construction phase' and logs materials and appliance warranties for life. A transfer at sale is a selling point to members (a documented-care home) and a warm lead for the buyer. Impact: Medium (acquisition, retention).
ideas.before: Record ends when a member moves
ideas.after: 'Transfer to Buyer' sends the full visit history and warranties; buyer gets an offer to keep the plan

ideas.title: Install Prompt Right After Sign-In
ideas.why: GoatCounter shows 13 Home Guide sign-ins but only 1 open of the add-to-home-screen option. web.dev says sign-in flows are a good, low-disruption place for an install promotion, as long as it's dismissible and remembered. Edits would go to preview.html first, live only after Max approves.
ideas.before: Add-to-home-screen option is easy to miss (1 open vs 13 sign-ins)
ideas.after: Small, dismissible 'Keep this guide on your phone' card just below sign-in

source.title: web.dev: Patterns for Promoting PWA Installation

ideas.title: Shutoffs and Emergency Info That Work Offline
ideas.why: Shutoffs and Emergency pages already get views, and those are exactly what a homeowner needs when power or internet is out. The published repo has a web manifest but no service worker; the offline cookbook shows how to cache key pages on install so they open with no connection.
steps: Add a service worker to the guide
Cache Shutoffs, Emergency, and Call pages on install
Serve from cache, falling back to network
Test in airplane mode on a phone

source.title: web.dev: Common Techniques to Build Offline Applications

ideas.title: Automatic Recall Check for Home Appliances
ideas.why: HomeAlmanac checks a homeowner's appliances against published safety recalls and flags any match. The US CPSC offers a free public Recalls API (JSON or XML) searchable by product name, so a membership app could check each logged appliance and alert the member, which is a clear, tangible perk for US homes.

ideas.title: Snap the Label, Skip the Typing
ideas.why: Homer, HomeMemory, eeva, and HomeAlmanac all let owners photograph an appliance nameplate and have the app read model and serial, then attach the manual and warranty. The planned quote app already takes model/serial photos, so auto-reading them would be the next step and is now table stakes among competitors.
mockup: Point camera at water heater label

ideas.title: Send Maintenance Tasks to My Calendar
ideas.why: eeva syncs renewals, tasks, and maintenance to Google, iCloud, or Outlook calendars. Putting reminders where members already look could raise follow-through without building a notification system first.

ideas.title: Show Only The Next Five Tasks
ideas.why: HouseSpouse's Home screen shows the next task plus a few coming up, five at most, with one-tap Done, Snooze, or Reschedule, so members feel ahead instead of buried.

ideas.title: Seasonal HVAC Tune-Up Reminders
ideas.why: ENERGY STAR advises a cooling check-up in spring and a heating check-up in fall, timed around the clock changes, and checking the air filter monthly (change at least every three months).
steps: Spring: book the cooling check-up
Every month: check the air filter
Every 3 months at most: change the filter
Fall: book the heating check-up

ideas.title: Free Tier Plus Shareable Schedule
ideas.why: SeasonKeep offers one home free with no card, then a paid plan adding history, cost tracking, a shareable read-only schedule, and CSV export. A similar ladder could lower the barrier to a Home Record membership.
ideas.before: Paid membership is the only way in
ideas.after: Free starter schedule; paid adds history, sharing, export

ideas.title: Summary First, Details On Tap
ideas.why: NN/g's progressive disclosure guidance: show the most important options first and reveal specialized ones on request, which improves learnability, efficiency, and error rate.
ideas.before: Every brief shows full text at once
ideas.after: One-line summary per tile; tap to expand

ideas.title: Native Share Sheet For Results
ideas.why: The Web Share API lets web apps open the phone's own share sheet for text and links; it needs a user tap and HTTPS, and support varies, so feature-detect and keep a fallback.
